calls.result:
The spec is written and lints clean (100/100). It's a spec-only bundle, so there is no Dafny contract. It needs your approval before I write any code.

**Bundle:** `forgemyspec-bundle/mini-os/spec.yaml`

| Obligation | Kind | What it checks |
|---|---|---|
| `boot_sector_layout` | boundary | The first 512 bytes of `os.img` are the boot sector, and bytes 510–511 are `0x55 0xAA`. |
| `freestanding_kernel` | boundary | The kernel compiles with `-ffreestanding -nostdlib` and has no libc includes or undefined symbols. |
| `vga_driver` | boundary | The kernel writes 80×25 character-plus-attribute cells at `0xB8000`. |
| `qemu_boot_banner` | boundary | A headless `qemu-system-i386` run leaves the banner text in VGA memory. |

**Assumptions**
- It's a 32-bit x86 BIOS boot with no UEFI.
- The tools `nasm`, `i686-elf-gcc` and `qemu-system-i386` are on PATH. I found all three here.
- The kernel fits in at most 32 sectors, so the boot sector can load it.

**Out of scope:** interrupts, keyboard input, paging, filesystem, userspace and any driver other than VGA text.

**Planned files:** `os/boot.asm`, `os/kernel.c`, `os/linker.ld`, `Makefile`, `tests_os/` and a `README.md`.

**To approve:** type the code **TA7NTV** in the chat. After that I'll run `approve`, implement the OS and run the gate.

calls.result:
The OS is built and the gate passes (`RESULT: PASS`). It is a 32-bit BIOS system that boots in QEMU and prints a banner through VGA text memory at `0xB8000`.

The gate's 4 boundary tests all pass, including a headless QEMU boot that reads the banner back out of VGA memory. The requirements board is empty because I never added this request to `forgemyspec-board.yaml`.

- **Bootloader (`os/boot.asm`):** a 512-byte boot sector ending in `0x55AA`. It loads the kernel with a BIOS extended disk read and switches to protected mode. If the disk read fails, it prints "Disk read error".
- **Kernel (`os/kernel.c`):** freestanding C with no includes and no undefined symbols. It clears the screen, writes characters with attributes, handles newlines and scrolls at row 25. It then prints "MiniOS 0.1 - booted in 32-bit protected mode" and halts.
- **Build files:** `Makefile`, `os/linker.ld`, `README.md` and `tests_os/test_os.py`.

To use it, run `make run` (or `make`, which builds without booting). The image is `os/build/os.img`, not `./os.img` as the spec implies.

The guard rejected my first build commands because the spec doesn't list the image path. I didn't try to get around that: I moved the build output under `os/build/`, which the spec does cover. Putting `os.img` at the repo root would need a spec amendment, which would need your re-approval.

I also fixed two bugs in my own tests while getting the gate to pass: the QEMU monitor needs the dump path in quotes, and a stale half-built kernel was being reused until I ran `make clean`.
